claims.head: The Golden Knights should tilt the ice
claims.body: The Golden Knights have been near the top of the league at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Sharks one of the worst. Expect the Golden Knights to spend more of the night in the Sharks’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

notes.text: Noah Hanifin is on injured reserve and has missed the last 5 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Parker Wotherspoon has taken his spot beside Dylan Coghlan. That pair has had 65% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 58:59 together, up from 43% with Hanifin.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 29% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the second-lowest in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Igor Chernyshov is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 13 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Michael Misa has taken his spot beside Will Smith and Macklin Celebrini. That line has had 44% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 53:03 together, down from 60% with Chernyshov.
Kiefer Sherwood is out week to week (upper body injury) and missed their last game.
Alexander Wennberg returned in their last game after missing 2 games.

stakes: The Sharks go in fourth in the Pacific with 22 points, 9 points behind the Golden Knights, second.

SJS.head: The Golden Knights should be favored
SJS.body: Even though San Jose has home-ice advantage, Vegas has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and gets Hanifin back. To pull this off, the Sharks can start with keeping shots to a minimum, plus Yaroslav Askarov stealing the show.

story.head: Stone’s favorite opponent
paras: The Sharks (10-12-2) lost 5-2 to Calgary on Nov 17, and the Golden Knights are winless in four (0-1-3). This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Golden Knights second (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Sharks fourth (tied for 20th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.
The Golden Knights’ record (.646) is about what their chances are worth. The Sharks’ record (.458) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.399), largely thanks to their goaltending.
This season, the Golden Knights have outscored teams 79-68, but only 49-46 at 5-on-5. On special teams, they’ve outscored teams 24-16.

The Golden Knights draw more penalties than they take (1st), have one of the league’s best penalty kills (2nd) and create chances on the penalty kill (2nd). On the other side, the Sharks do a lot of their shooting from distance (2nd lowest) and ice the puck a lot (32nd). They also are one of the league’s most physical teams (2nd), so expect a chippy, heavy game. The Knights’ power play (4th) could do real damage against the Sharks’ penalty kill (30th).

Jack Eichel (9 G / 20 A / 29 P in 24 GP) leads the Golden Knights in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, with a point in nine straight games against San Jose. Mark Stone (11 G / 11 A / 22 P in 24 GP) has a team-high eleven goals. The Sharks’ scoring runs through Macklin Celebrini (9 G / 18 A / 27 P in 22 GP), and Will Smith (8 G / 11 A / 19 P in 24 GP) is next in line.

Yaroslav Askarov (6-9-1 / .888 SV% in 16 GS) will likely start for San Jose. Vegas has two options in net: Adin Hill (7-2-3 / .898 SV% in 12 GS) and Carter Hart (6-4-2 / .888 SV% in 12 GS). Hill has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Nov 19. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
The Golden Knights usually control more of the chances than the Sharks do.

items.text: The Golden Knights have been without Noah Hanifin since Nov 8.
The Sharks are newly without Kiefer Sherwood, and have been without Igor Chernyshov since Oct 22.
Victor Olofsson has eight goals on chances worth about 3.4 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
Mason Marchment and Will Smith have a point in four straight games.
